feed.title: Emotion of the day · Follow or Bounce
feed.subtitle: One emotion a day from the Dictionary of Inner Experience.

entry.title: Attachment
entry.summary: Security and bond rather than active positive feeling in the moment — you can be attached to someone you are currently angry at.

entry.title: Desire
entry.summary: Wanting, which can exist with or without Love and is closer to an impulse than a discrete emotion.

entry.title: Pride
entry.summary: A sense of the self's expansion or elevation following a valued achievement or quality, recognized as one's own.

entry.title: Surprise
entry.summary: A brief orienting reaction to an unexpected event, valence-neutral until appraisal resolves it toward pleasant or unpleasant. Its status as a true emotion versus a pre-emotional reflex is genuinely disputed in the literature.

entry.title: Antipathy
entry.summary: A settled dislike or aversion toward someone or something, milder and more passive than Hatred.

entry.title: Anxiety
entry.summary: A sustained state of tension and worry without one clear, immediate object — diffuse, future-oriented, and cognitively elaborated, unlike Fear's sharp present focus.

entry.title: Rejection
entry.summary: The painful appraisal of having been excluded or refused by someone whose acceptance mattered.

entry.title: Affection
entry.summary: A lighter, warmer, lower-stakes fondness than Love, without requiring its depth or duration.

entry.title: Loneliness
entry.summary: The painful, subjective sense of lacking wanted connection — unlike Isolation, which can be neutral, and Solitude, which can be chosen.

entry.title: Rumination
entry.summary: Repetitive, unresolved dwelling on a distressing thought or event, which sustains rather than processes the feeling behind it.

entry.title: Guilt
entry.summary: A response to a specific action judged wrong, oriented toward repair rather than hiding.

entry.title: Euphoria
entry.summary: Joy at an intensity that can feel disorienting, often driven by exertion, relief, or a physiological cause rather than an ordinary event.

entry.title: Longing
entry.summary: A sustained wanting directed at something distant or unattainable, without Nostalgia's specific orientation to the past.

entry.title: Trust
entry.summary: A settled expectation that another person or system will not cause harm, allowing reliance without constant vigilance.

entry.title: Bewilderment
entry.summary: Confusion that blocks action or decision — you don't know what to do next.

entry.title: Affection
entry.summary: A lighter, warmer, lower-stakes fondness than Love, without requiring its depth or duration.

entry.title: Low Mood
entry.summary: A sustained, diffuse state of low energy and flat affect with an open causal story, distinguished from the regulation strategy of Suppression that the source dictionary had bundled into it.

entry.title: Joy
entry.summary: A response to something appraised as good, moderate to high in activation, and tied to a specific moment rather than sustained.

entry.title: Humiliation
entry.summary: Shame imposed from outside by another's action — involuntary, public, and other-caused, often carrying anger at the humiliator alongside the shame.

entry.title: Irritation
entry.summary: Anger at low intensity, usually triggered by repeated minor friction rather than one clear wrong.

entry.title: Emptiness
entry.summary: A reactive, often post-intensity depletion — tired and hollow after something, with a proximate cause, unlike Void's chronic and causeless register.

entry.title: Joy
entry.summary: A response to something appraised as good, moderate to high in activation, and tied to a specific moment rather than sustained.

entry.title: Rage
entry.summary: Anger at an intensity that overrides self-control.

entry.title: Absurdity
entry.summary: The felt clash between a search for meaning and a world that offers no confirming answer.

entry.title: Devotion
entry.summary: Sustained commitment and action toward someone or something, which can outlast the felt intensity of Love itself.

entry.title: Solitude
entry.summary: A chosen, often restorative state of being alone, without the pain that defines Loneliness.

entry.title: Longing
entry.summary: A sustained wanting directed at something distant or unattainable, without Nostalgia's specific orientation to the past.

entry.title: Alienation
entry.summary: A sense of estrangement from a group, place, or one's own experience, broader and more existential than momentary Loneliness.

entry.title: Humiliation
entry.summary: Shame imposed from outside by another's action — involuntary, public, and other-caused, often carrying anger at the humiliator alongside the shame.

entry.title: Resentment
entry.summary: Anger that has moved from a single episode into a lasting disposition, usually directed at a specific person with a sense of accumulated unfairness.
